extraction.name: RoboBench
extraction.description: A benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains across five dimensions: instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis.
extraction.creator: Yulin Luo, Chun-Kai Fan, Menghang Dong, Jiayu Shi, Mengdi Zhao, Bo-Wen Zhang, Cheng Chi, Jiaming Liu, Gaole Dai, Rongyu Zhang, Ruichuan An, Kun Wu, Zhengping Che, Shaoxuan Xie, Guocai Yao, Zhongxia Zhao, Pengwei Wang, Guang Liu, Zhongyuan Wang, Tiejun Huang, Shanghang Zhang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Datasets are built from open-source and in-house robotic data, enriched with MLLM- and human-provided annotations, aligning each sub-benchmark with the embodied task pipeline.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Large-scale real-world robotic datasets combined with curated in-house collection.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Implicit instructions are obtained by rewriting explicit instructions into demand-based requests using LLMs. Planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: General and task-specific filters were applied, addressing image quality and task validity, with tailored rules such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Structured annotations (task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata) are generated by Gemini and then refined by human annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Quality inspections were conducted by 20 professionally trained annotators to validate linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness. A majority-vote strategy was adopted where items solved correctly by all models were removed, and items failed by all models underwent manual review.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 professionally trained annotators / expert annotators (with prior training)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset relies on synthesized planning-level failures due to a lack of real-world planning failure data. Additionally, existing planning data primarily focuses on concrete action execution without explicitly distinguishing between left-right arm assignments or positional movements.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluating Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) as embodied brains for robotic manipulation.

name.evidence: ROBOBENCH: A COMPREHENSIVEEVALUATION BENCHMARK FORMULTIMODALLARGELANGUAGE MODELS ASEMBODIEDBRAIN

description.evidence: To bridge this gap, we introduce RoboBench, a benchmark that systematically evaluates multimodal large language models (MLLMs) as embodied brains. Motivated by the critical roles across the full manipulation pipeline, RoboBench defines five dimensions—instruction comprehension, perception reasoning, generalized planning, affordance prediction, and failure analysis—spanning 14 capabilities, 25 tasks, and 6092 QA pairs.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Explicit instructions are drawn from daily-life scenarios with clearly specified actions and targets, whereas implicit instructions are obtained by rewriting them into demand-based requests using LLMs... planning-level failures are synthesized by perturbing correct instructions (wrong object, missing step, wrong order) due to lack of real-world planning failure data.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: We apply both general and task-specific filters. General criteria address image quality and task validity, while sub-benchmarks have tailored rules—such as excluding single-arm data from dual-arm tasks.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: Gemini Comanici et al. (2025) generates structured annotations—task summaries, step-wise instructions with timestamps, and metadata (objects, actions, scenes, embodiments)—which are refined by human annotators.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: After data construction, we recruite 20 professionally trained annotators to conduct comprehensive quality inspections, validating linguistic clarity, answerability, and correctness Liu et al. (2024d). We further adopt a majority-vote strategy Liu et al. (2024d): items that all models solve correctly are removed, whereas items all models fail to solve undergo manual review and correction.
